messages.subject: Re: Changing the column positions of an xdf dataset
messages.subject_clean: Changing the column positions of an xdf dataset
messages.body_plain:
Hi Raffie,

This question relates to Revolution R Enterprise, not Revolution R Open. You can get your question answered by asking the Technical Support Team (if you have a Support subscription) or by posting to the Revolution R Enterprise forums at:

https://revolutionanalytics.zendesk.com/forums

Kind regards,
# David Smith

On Saturday, February 28, 2015 at 1:56:07 AM UTC-6, Raffie Roslan wrote:
>
> I would like to know if there is a way to reorder the column positions of an xdf dataset. For example, if I have an xdf dataset with columns [,a],[,c],[,b], I would like to reorder the columns to [,a],[,b],[,c] without having to create a dataframe, reorder the columns, and use RxImport or rxDataFrameToXdf to convert it back to an xdf file (because the xdf file potentially has 100s of millions of rows and I don't want to write the dataset to memory).
>
> One potential solution I see is using the rxSetVarInfoXdf function, which has information on the column position.
> Something like:
> #Swap positions for columns 2 and 3
> varInfo <- list(list(position = 2, position = 3), list(position = 3, position = 2))
>
> But this will not work as position is a value which you call to reference the column but not to change it.

messages.body_plain:
Dear David Smith,

I actually have encountered this issue in the OS X version of RRO 8.0.1 beta2 simply by trying to load a library, specifically package HH that I need for a class this semester.  I'm brand new to R and very excited to learn about as I use SAS every day at work, yet this is my first experience with the software.

Here is exactly what my console showed from installing the package (using the latest URL, simply running install.packages(HH) provided the URL for 3.1-5 whereas the latest version is 3.1-15 -- please note that neither work, and both provide the same error) through attempting to load if with library(HH).

Any help you can provide would be greatly appreciated.

messages.subject: RRO version
messages.body_plain:
How do I find which version of RRO is installed, and how can I be sure that RStudio is running RRO and not R?

Today (2015-03-29). I thought I had downloaded and installed RRO 8.0.1 built on R 3.1.2 onto my mac (OS 10.10 Yosemite) running RStudio (version 0.98.1103) - after having sent the previously installed R 3.1.3 to the trash. However, when I run "Revolution R Open" or RStudio they bring up R 3.1.3, not R 3.1.2, and there is no indication that it is, in fact, RRO that is running.

Is this what I should expect, or do I need to delete everything and start over?

messages.subject: RRO 8.0.1, gfortran, packages (was RRO version)
messages.body_plain:
I removed RRO 8.0.1 and reinstalled R, but cannot install all the packages that had been previously successfully installed in R. Below, is the description of what I’ve done and the results (MAC OS X 10.10 Yosemite, 16G RAM).

I completely uninstalled RRO 8.0.1:

   cd /Applications

   sudo rm -rf "Revolution R Open".app

   cd /Library/Frameworks

   sudo rm -rf R.framework

   sudo rm /usr/bin/R

   sudo rm /usr/bin/Rscript

And completely removed R 3.1.3:

   rm -rf /Library/Frameworks/R.framework /Applications/R.app \

      /usr/bin/R /usr/bin/Rscript

And completely removed RStudio:

   mv ~/.rstudio-desktop ~/backup-rstudio-desktop

And moved any R, RStudio and RRO icons to the trash.

Then, I reinstalled RRO 8.0.1, this time successfully. But, there were quite a number of packages that threw warnings or error messages and I couldn’t load many of the libraries. In particular, I could not install the package tsinterp which I had previously successfully installed on R 3.1.3, but not without some preliminary steps which were:

   From the Appstore:

      Install or update Xcode

   Install Fortran from the following from the terminal:

      curl -O http://r.research.att.com/libs/gfortran-4.8.2-darwin13.tar.bz2

      sudo tar fvxz gfortran-4.8.2-darwin13.tar.bz2 -C /

Install the following packages in R:

      install.packages("httr")

      library(httr)

      install.packages("bitops")

      library(httr)

      install.packages("devtools")

      library(devtools)

         Sys.setenv(MAKEFLAGS = "-j4")

         source('http://mc-stan.org/rstan/install.R', echo = TRUE, max.deparse.length = 2000)

         library(rstan)

   Download and install tsinterp and its dependency multitaper:

      devtools::install_github("wesleyburr/tsinterp")

Doing the above on a new installation of RRO 8.0.1 did successfully install multitaper, but not tsinterp, and resulted in the following warnings and error messages:

devtools::install_github("wesleyburr/tsinterp")

Downloading github repo wesleyburr/tsinterp@master

Installing tsinterp

'/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/bin/R' --vanilla CMD  \

  --library='/Users/claireaustin/Library/R/3.1/library'  \

  --install-tests

* installing *source* package ‘tsinterp’ ...

** libs

gfortran-4.8   -fPIC  -g -O2  -c dpofa.f -o dpofa.o

gfortran-4.8   -fPIC  -g -O2  -c dposl.f -o dposl.o

gfortran-4.8: warning: couldn’t understand kern.osversion ‘14.0.0

gfortran-4.8: warning: couldn’t understand kern.osversion ‘14.0.0

clang -dynamiclib -Wl,-headerpad_max_install_names -undefined dynamic_lookup -single_module -multiply_defined suppress -L/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/lib -L/usr/local/lib -o tsinterp.so dpofa.o dposl.o -L/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/lib -lRlapack -L/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/lib -lRblas -L/usr/local/lib/gcc/x86_64-apple-darwin13.0.0/4.8.2 -lgfortran -lquadmath -lm -L/usr/local/lib/gcc/x86_64-apple-darwin13.0.0/4.8.2 -lgfortran -lquadmath -lm -F/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/.. -framework R -Wl,-framework -Wl,CoreFoundation

installing to /Users/claireaustin/Library/R/3.1/library/tsinterp/libs

** R

** help

*** installing help indices

** building package indices

Error in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...) :

  unable to load shared object '/Users/claireaustin/Library/R/3.1/library/tsinterp/libs/tsinterp.so':

  dlopen(/Users/claireaustin/Library/R/3.1/library/tsinterp/libs/tsinterp.so, 6): Symbol not found: ___addtf3

  Referenced from: /usr/local/lib/libquadmath.0.dylib

Error: loading failed

So, I completely removed RRO 8.0.1 again, reinstalled R 3.1.3 and RStudio 0.98.11030.98.1103, updated all the packages, and tried to reinstall the package tsinterp in R 3.1.3 as described above (which, remember, I had successfully done in R 3.1.3 before installing RRO 8.0.1 the first time), but got the same warnings and error messages as when I had tried to install tsinterp in RRO 8.0.1.

Now I’m left with a bit of a mess and any suggestions on how to fix it would be very welcome. Thanks. Claire
